samples.summary: Removing the `quoted` bail-out in `replacePrefixes` leaves quoted lines that the new, stricter `QUOTE_RE` does not match unprotected — the old `- > x` corruption comes back for them
samples.evidence: The removed guard used `QUOTED_RE = /^\s*>/` (any amount of leading whitespace before the `>`). Its replacement, `packages/notes/src/view/list-commands.ts:45` `QUOTE_RE = /^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/`, only admits up to three leading spaces. A legitimate markdown line such as `    > quoted` (a blockquote nested inside a two-level list item, indent 4) now parses with `quote === ''` and `content === '> quoted'`, and `replacePrefixes` (list-commands.ts:228-237, the `if (p.quoted) continue;` skip deleted) happily writes a marker in front of it, producing `    - > quoted` — exactly the corruption #925 added the skip to prevent. Same for a tab after the marker (`>\t- a`): `> ?` matches only a space, so the tab falls into `indent` and `shift()` (list-commands.ts:309-310) silently rewrites it as spaces. No test in list-commands.test.ts covers a >3-space or tab-separated quote prefix.

samples.summary: Three different definitions of "blockquote prefix" now exist in the notes view layer and disagree about what they match
samples.evidence: `packages/notes/src/view/commands.ts:278` (`toggleQuote`) uses `QUOTE_RE = /^\s*>\s?/`; `packages/notes/src/view/list-commands.ts:45` now uses `/^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/`; `packages/notes/src/view/checkbox-input.ts:9` uses a third form `( {0,3}(?:> ?)*\s*)`. They diverge on unlimited leading whitespace, on a tab after `>`, and on multiple `>` markers — `toggleQuote` unquoting `   > - a` strips `   > ` (indent included) whereas the list commands treat `   > ` as the quote and everything after it as indent. Nothing shares a constant, so the three will drift further; a single exported prefix matcher would keep the Quote button, the list commands and the checkbox input handler in step.

samples.summary: `isBlank` semantics changed for quote-only lines, which changes what `computeActiveFormats`/the toolbar reports for a mixed selection
samples.evidence: With the quote prefix now peeled off in `parseLine`, a line consisting of just `> ` has `content === ''` and so `isBlank(p)` (list-commands.ts:99-101) is now true, where before it was false (`content` was the whole `> ` text). `targetLines` (list-commands.ts:128-131) therefore drops such lines from the target set, so `computeListState` — read by `computeActiveFormats` at packages/notes/src/view/commands.ts:65 and rendered as pressed/disabled state in packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-toolbar.tsx:316 — now reports the kind of the surrounding lines for a selection that includes an empty quoted line, and list toggles skip that line instead of marking it up. Probably benign, but it is an unasserted behaviour change in an exported reader's contract; no test covers a selection containing a bare `> ` line.

finding.evidence: The removed guard used `QUOTED_RE = /^\s*>/` (any amount of leading whitespace before the `>`). A legitimate markdown line such as `    > quoted` (a blockquote nested inside a two-level list item, indent 4) now parses with `quote === ''` and `content === '> quoted'`, and `replacePrefixes` (list-commands.ts:228-237, the `if (p.quoted) continue;` skip deleted) happily writes a marker in front of it, producing `    - > quoted` — exactly the corruption #925 added the skip to prevent. verdict.reason: The behaviour described is factually real — I reproduced it by reading the code: QUOTE_RE at list-commands.ts:45 is `/^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/`, so `    > quoted` parses with quote='' / indent='    ' / content='> quoted' (parseLine, :49-74), and toggleKind/replacePrefixes (:284-289, :224-253, which contain no `quoted` skip) writes `    - > quoted`; the tab case at :306-311 also holds. But it is out of the blast-radius lane. Every cited location is inside the one changed file, in module-private code: grep for `parseLine` / `ParsedLine` / `replacePrefixes` finds no source consumer outside packages/notes/src/view/list-commands.ts (only .agent-review artefacts and unrelated node_modules). There is no second entry point reaching the mutation — the only other prefix writer, setTaskChecked (:332-350), returns early on `p.check === null`, which is the case for such a line. No caller, export, signature, or cross-package contract is broken. The finding is statable without leaving the diff and reduces to "the new regex condition is too narrow", which this lens explicitly defers to the correctness lens ("Logic inside the diff — wrong conditions... That is the correctness lens"). Refuted on lane only; the defect itself is genuine and belongs to correctness, not dismissed as unreal.
